cīvis, cīvis m./f.

noun, third declension, masculine or feminine

a citizen, man or woman

A member of a state with its rights, against a foreigner (peregrīnus) or an enemy (hostis), of either sex (Lewis & Short). Citizenship is cīvitās (Traupman 178); my fellow citizens, cīvēs meī (Traupman 291); a citizen who holds no office, prīvātus (see individual).

Other words

  • cīvitās, cīvitātis f. — citizenship

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. cīvitās: citizenship, the rights of a citizen; Traupman 178; Traupman 291

Examples

  • Rōmānus sum … cīvis; C. Mūcium vocant.

    I am a Roman citizen; my name is Gaius Mucius.Liv. 2.12.9

  • cīvēs meī

    my fellow citizensTraupman 291

See also state, individual, community, city.
